songInfo.title: You Give Love a Bad Name

scalesUsed.notes: C - D - Eb - F - G - Ab - Bb - C
scalesUsed.application: Primary scale for harmony and melody; the minor tonality gives the verses their dark, aggressive edge
Guitar solo and lead fills; the pentatonic framework drives the solo's rock energy

scalesUsed.notes: C - Eb - F - Gb - G - Bb
scalesUsed.application: Chromatic passing tones in the solo and unison bends add bluesy grit

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aeolian (Natural Minor) with anthemic power chord delivery
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C minor is the relative minor of Eb major

mainProgression.description: Classic minor key arena rock progression using the natural minor chords to create an anthemic yet dark sound. The VI-VII-III movement provides an uplifting quality against the minor tonic.

sectionProgressions.description: The iconic unaccompanied vocal chorus opening - one of rock's most dramatic intros with the full band crashing in on the repeat
Driving palm-muted power chords with syncopated accents, creating a tight, aggressive feel beneath the vocal
Building energy with ascending chord motion, lifting toward the explosive chorus

sectionProgressions.progression: Cm - Ab - Bb - Eb - Ab - Bb - Cm
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - VI - VII - III - VI - VII - i
sectionProgressions.description: The massive singalong chorus with full open power chords and the III chord adding brightness to the minor key

sectionProgressions.progression: Ab - Bb - Cm - Ab - Bb - G
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: VI - VII - i - VI - VII - V
sectionProgressions.description: The bridge introduces the dominant V chord (G major) for dramatic tension before the guitar solo

harmonicFunction: Cm (i) - Minor tonic providing the dark, aggressive foundation
Ab (VI) - Submediant major chord, creating warmth and anthemic lift within the minor key
Bb (VII) - Subtonic major chord, building momentum and forward drive toward resolution
Eb (III) - Mediant major (relative major), providing brightness in the chorus
G (V) - Dominant chord in the bridge, creating classical tension for the solo entrance

techniques.name: Power Chord Rhythm with Syncopated Accents
techniques.description: The backbone of the song - driving eighth-note power chord rhythm with punchy palm-muted accents on syncopated beats, creating the aggressive arena rock feel

notes: C5: X-3-5-5-X-X (root 5th string power chord at 3rd fret)
Ab5: 4-6-6-X-X-X (root 6th string power chord at 4th fret)
Bb5: 6-8-8-X-X-X (root 6th string power chord at 6th fret)
Eb5: X-6-8-8-X-X (root 5th string power chord at 6th fret)
Syncopated accents fall on the 'and' of beat 2 and beat 4
Palm muting between accented hits creates the chugging rhythm
sequence: Start with palm-muted eighth notes on C5
Accent specific beats by lifting the palm mute for punchy stabs
Slide up the neck from C5 to Eb5 using the same shape
Move to the 6th string root for Ab5 and Bb5 changes
tips: The syncopated accents are what make this riff exciting - practice them with a metronome
Keep your palm muting light enough to still hear the pitch, not just percussive thud
The power chord shapes slide easily up and down the neck - use this to your advantage
Lock in with the kick drum pattern for tight rhythmic precision
details.progression: C5 - Ab5 - Bb5 - C5 (i - VI - VII - i)

techniques.name: Palm Muting Technique
techniques.description: Controlled palm muting throughout the verses to create dynamic contrast with the wide-open chorus power chords, essential for capturing the song's aggressive energy

notes: Rest the fleshy edge of the picking hand lightly on the strings near the bridge
Alternate between fully muted chugging and accented open hits
The verse sections are predominantly palm-muted for a tight, controlled sound
The chorus lifts the muting entirely for maximum power and sustain
sequence: Position palm at the bridge saddles for optimal muting contact
Play palm-muted eighth notes on the root power chord
Lift palm on accented beats for dynamic punch
Remove palm muting completely when transitioning to the chorus
Return to tight muting for the next verse
tips: Hand position is critical - too far forward kills the sustain, too far back loses the mute
Practice the contrast between muted and open sections until it feels natural
The transition from muted verse to open chorus is the song's primary dynamic tool
Use the bridge pickup for maximum definition on palm-muted notes
details.progression: Palm-muted C5 with open accents on Ab5 and Bb5

techniques.name: Unison Bends and Solo Phrasing
techniques.description: The guitar solo features expressive unison bends where a bent note on one string matches the pitch of an unbent note on an adjacent string, combined with pentatonic rock phrasing

notes: Unison bend: Bend the G string at the 8th fret (C to D) to match the B string at the 6th fret (Eb bent sounds like the open note)
Based primarily on C minor pentatonic in the 8th position
Whole-step bends on the B and G strings for expressive phrasing
Vibrato applied to sustained bent notes for emotional impact
sequence: Position in the C minor pentatonic box at the 8th fret
Execute the unison bend by fretting both the G and B strings simultaneously
Bend the lower string up to match the pitch of the higher string
Apply vibrato while holding the bend for sustain
Release and continue the pentatonic phrase
tips: Use your ring finger backed by the middle and index fingers for bend strength
Listen carefully to ensure the bent note matches the target pitch exactly
Practice the unison bend isolated before incorporating it into phrases
Richie Sambora's solo is melodic rather than shredding - focus on singing quality
details.progression: Solo over Cm - Ab - Bb - Cm progression

sections.name: A Cappella Intro
sections.description: One of rock's most iconic openings - the entire band drops out for an a cappella vocal chorus that immediately hooks the listener before the instruments crash in
notes: No guitar in this section - the vocal carries the melody alone
Use this time to prepare for the explosive band entrance
The vocal melody outlines the Cm - Ab - Bb - Cm progression
Count along to lock in with the tempo before the instruments hit

sections.name: Verse
sections.technique: Power Chord Rhythm with Syncopated Accents
sections.description: Tight, palm-muted power chord rhythm with syncopated accents driving underneath the vocal with aggressive arena rock energy
notes: Heavy palm muting throughout for a tight, controlled rhythm
Syncopated accents on the 'and' of beats 2 and 4 create the driving feel
Keep the dynamics restrained compared to the chorus
The guitar locks in tightly with the bass and kick drum pattern

sections.name: Pre-Chorus
sections.technique: Power Chord Rhythm with Syncopated Accents
sections.description: Building section with ascending chord motion lifting the energy from the tight verse toward the explosive chorus
notes: Reduce palm muting gradually as the section builds
Strumming intensity increases with each chord change
The ascending Ab-Bb-Cm motion creates natural energy buildup
Let the final Cm ring slightly longer before the chorus hits

sections.name: Chorus
sections.technique: Power Chord Rhythm with Syncopated Accents
sections.description: The massive arena singalong chorus - 'Shot through the heart!' - with full open power chords at maximum intensity and the Eb chord adding brightness
sections.progression: Cm - Ab - Bb - Eb - Ab - Bb - Cm
notes: Lift all palm muting for maximum sustain and power
The Eb (III) chord adds a bright, uplifting quality to the minor key chorus
Full downstroke attack on every chord for arena-filling power
This is the dynamic peak - play with maximum conviction and energy

sections.name: Bridge
sections.technique: Power Chord Rhythm with Syncopated Accents
sections.description: The bridge section introduces the dominant G chord for dramatic tension, creating a darker mood before launching into the guitar solo
sections.progression: Ab - Bb - Cm - Ab - Bb - G
notes: The G major chord (V) is new here and creates classical dominant tension
The bridge pulls back slightly in dynamics before building to the solo
Hold the final G chord with a slight ritardando into the solo entrance
This is the emotional pivot point of the song

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Richie Sambora's melodic guitar solo using C minor pentatonic with signature unison bends and expressive vibrato over the verse chord progression
notes: Solo primarily uses C minor pentatonic at the 8th position
Signature unison bends on the G and B strings are the highlight
Phrasing is melodic and vocal-like rather than technical shredding
Wide vibrato on sustained notes adds emotional weight

sections.name: Final Chorus
sections.technique: Power Chord Rhythm with Syncopated Accents
sections.description: Extended final chorus with repeated 'shot through the heart' hook, building to maximum arena intensity with the full band locked in
sections.progression: Cm - Ab - Bb - Eb - Ab - Bb - Cm
notes: Maximum energy and sustain throughout the final chorus
Repeated chorus hook builds crowd participation energy
The ending resolves firmly on the Cm power chord
Slight ritardando on the final hit for a dramatic ending

alternatives: Any HSS or HH configured guitar
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for rhythm power chords; combined positions for lead tone warmth

settings.treble: 7 (bright and cutting for power chord definition)
settings.bass: 5 (tight low end to support fast rhythms)

effects.distortion: Marshall JCM800 natural overdrive with optional boost pedal (Boss SD-1 or similar) for the solo section
effects.delay: Short digital delay (250-350ms) for lead tone thickening during solo
effects.reverb: Medium hall reverb for the 1980s arena rock ambiance
effects.other: Chorus pedal (subtle) for clean arpeggiated passages; noise gate recommended for tight palm-muted sections

beginner.focus: Learn the basic power chord shapes and the main chord progression
steps: Master the C5, Ab5, Bb5, and Eb5 power chord shapes
Practice the i-VI-VII-i progression slowly with downstrokes
Work on basic palm muting technique with a single power chord
Play along with the chorus section at reduced tempo

intermediate.focus: Add syncopated accents, palm muting dynamics, and full song structure
steps: Develop the syncopated accent pattern over palm-muted rhythm
Practice dynamic contrast between muted verse and open chorus
Learn the bridge section with its new G chord
Play through the complete song structure with backing track
intermediate.timeEstimate: 3-4 weeks for complete rhythm guitar performance

advanced.focus: Master the guitar solo, unison bends, and performance dynamics
steps: Learn the C minor pentatonic scale at the 8th position
Practice unison bends and wide vibrato technique
Work through the complete solo at half speed, building up gradually
Combine rhythm and lead roles for a full performance

commonMistakes: Missing the syncopated accents and playing straight eighth notes instead
Not enough dynamic contrast between the palm-muted verse and open chorus
Rushing the tempo during the energy buildup into the chorus
Unison bends not reaching the correct target pitch in the solo
practiceRoutine: Warm up with power chord shapes moving between C5, Ab5, Bb5, Eb5 (5 minutes)
Practice palm muting with syncopated accents at 100 BPM (5 minutes)
Work on the verse-to-chorus dynamic transition (5 minutes)
Practice unison bends and solo phrases isolated at slow tempo (5 minutes)
Full song run-through with backing track at 123 BPM (5 minutes)
focusAreas: Syncopated accent placement for the driving rhythm feel
Palm muting control and dynamic contrast between sections
Clean power chord transitions at tempo
Unison bend accuracy and vibrato control for the solo
metronomeWork: Start at 90 BPM with the basic power chord progression
Add syncopated accents at 100 BPM once chord changes are clean
Build to performance tempo of 123 BPM with full dynamics
Practice the solo phrases independently at 80 BPM before integrating
